## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

42	// requireSecureAssetURL gates every plugin HTTP fetch on a transport that a
43	// network attacker can't rewrite.
44	//
45	// Plaintext HTTP is not merely "less good" here: the asset and the
46	// checksums.txt that authenticates it come from the same origin, so an
47	// attacker who can rewrite one can rewrite both, and checksum verification
48	// becomes theatre. HTTPS is therefore required for anything off-machine.
49	//
50	// Loopback is exempt so httptest-backed tests and local forge experiments
51	// keep working — traffic that never leaves the machine has no network
52	// attacker to defend against.
53	func requireSecureAssetURL(rawURL string) error {
54		u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
55		if err != nil {
56			return fmt.Errorf("parse download URL %q: %w", redactURL(rawURL), err)
57		}
58		switch strings.ToLower(u.Scheme) {
59		case "https":
60			return nil
61		case "http":
62			if isLoopbackHost(u.Hostname()) {
63				return nil
64			}
65			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to download %s over plaintext HTTP: the asset and its %s would share an origin, so a network attacker could replace both and checksum verification would prove nothing; serve the release over HTTPS or declare an https download_url in %s",
66				redactURL(rawURL), checksumsFileName, pluginMetadataFileName)
67		default:
68			return fmt.Errorf("plugin downloads must use https; %q has scheme %q", redactURL(rawURL), u.Scheme)
69		}

72	// isLoopbackHost reports whether host addresses this machine.
73	func isLoopbackHost(host string) bool {
74		if strings.EqualFold(host, "localhost") {
75			return true
76		}
77		if ip := net.ParseIP(host); ip != nil {
78			return ip.IsLoopback()
79		}

content.text:
**The two errors** (both `goconst`, both in `cmd/entire/cli/plugin_fetch.go`):

```
plugin_fetch.go:59:7: string `https` has 3 occurrences, but such constant `schemeHTTPS` already exists
plugin_fetch.go:61:7: string `http`  has 3 occurrences, but such constant `schemeHTTP`  already exists
```

`login.go:25-26` already declares `schemeHTTP`/`schemeHTTPS` for the same package, so the literals just needed to use them. Fixed in the working tree:

- `plugin_fetch.go:59,61` — `case "https":` / `case "http":` → `case schemeHTTPS:` / `case schemeHTTP:`
- `plugin_fetch.go:124` — `u.Scheme != "https" && u.Scheme != "http"` → the constants
- `review_target.go:142` — same substitution

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` → **0 issues**. Package tests for the touched code pass.

## Why it only broke after the merge

This is a semantic merge conflict — neither side was wrong on its own, only their sum.

`goconst` counts occurrences **per package**, and its threshold is 3. The literals were split across two files that never existed at the same time until the merge:

| Commit | `plugin_fetch.go` | `review_target.go` | occurrences of `"https"` | lint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main before merge (`6e7985f4e`) | 2 (lines 59, 124) | absent | 2 | ✅ pass |
| trail branch head (`b989d612c`) | absent | 1 (line 142) | 1 | ✅ pass |
| merge (`f6fd1159d`) | 2 | 1 | **3** | ❌ fail |

Both parents were genuinely linted and genuinely green — the trail branch head has a successful `lint` check run, and main's previous push passed too. The timing is the whole story:

- The trail branch last merged main at `fbbff047` on **Aug 10, 08:38**.
- `plugin_fetch.go` landed on main at `18f9bcd9d` (PR #1422) on **Aug 10, 21:42** — about 13 hours later.

So the branch never had `plugin_fetch.go` in its tree, and main never had `review_target.go`. Nothing in either diff overlaps, so git merged cleanly, and only the merge commit's package hit 3.

Two things worth noting:

1. **`goconst` blames the wrong file.** It reported `plugin_fetch.go`, which was unchanged by the merge. The new code was `review_target.go`. That's expected behavior for a package-wide counter, but it makes the error look like a regression in code nobody touched.
2. **Nothing lints the merge result before it lands.** `.github/workflows/lint.yml` checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` — the branch head, not GitHub's merge ref. The push-to-main run is the first time the merged tree is ever linted, so any package-counting linter (`goconst`, `dupl`, `maintidx`) can only be caught after the fact. Switching the checkout to the default (the PR merge commit) would catch this class before merge; the tradeoff is that the run then depends on main moving underneath the PR.
